explanation: The proof is the contrapositive of the library's own lemma `Submodule.intCast_surjective_of_span_singleton_eq_top`. That lemma rests on another library lemma, `IsAddCyclic.intCast_surjective`, which is proved from Mathlib's `AddMonoidHom.map_addCyclic` and `Submodule.span_singleton_eq_top_iff`. I found nothing in Mathlib that says an additively cyclic ring, or a ring spanned over ℤ by a single element, has surjective `Int.cast`. I searched all uses of `IsAddCyclic` together with ring structure (`Cyclic.lean`, `Cyclic/Basic.lean`). I searched every `Function.Surjective (Int.cast …)` / `Surjective ((↑) : ℤ → …)` statement; the only hit is `ZMod.intCast_surjective`, which applies only to `ZMod n`. I also searched for `span_singleton_ne_top`; the only hit is `Ideal.span_singleton_ne_top`, which is about ideals and non-units. None of these gives the theorem in one or two short lines.
